curated_topic.selected_title: Claude Code sends your email address to websites
curated_topic.why_it_matters: This highlights a critical privacy trade-off in modern AI developer tools where personal identifiers are leaked to external sites during automated tasks. It forces a conversation about security defaults and user consent in the rapidly evolving AI CLI landscape.
curated_topic.hook_angle: Is your AI coding assistant leaking your identity without you knowing? A new discovery in Anthropic's Claude Code CLI has sparked a massive debate on where we should draw the line between 'helpful automation' and 'privacy violation.'

draft.hook: Imagine pushing a quick bug fix via CLI, only to realize the tool just broadcasted your private email to every domain it touched. Anthropic’s new Claude Code was caught doing exactly that.
key_takeaways: 🚨 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗸: Claude Code CLI sends your email address in the User-Agent header when fetching web content.
🛠️ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻: Anthropic says it helps site owners contact users if a bot misbehaves, but it’s active by default.
🛡️ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝘀𝗸: This turns a helpful assistant into a potential tracking vector for every site you scrape or analyze.
draft.discussion_question: 💬 Is "traceability" a valid excuse for leaking personal PII by default, or is this a major security oversight?
draft.full_post:
Imagine pushing a quick bug fix via CLI, only to realize the tool just broadcasted your private email to every domain it touched. Anthropic’s new Claude Code was caught doing exactly that.

🚨 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗸: Claude Code CLI sends your email address in the User-Agent header when fetching web content.

🛠️ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻: Anthropic says it helps site owners contact users if a bot misbehaves, but it’s active by default.

🛡️ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝘀𝗸: This turns a helpful assistant into a potential tracking vector for every site you scrape or analyze.

💬 Is "traceability" a valid excuse for leaking personal PII by default, or is this a major security oversight?

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/107757
